analysis.title: Multi-Asset Strategy Daily
key_insights: Midterms are the focus. Investors expect a Democratic sweep, with the Senate a closer call. The obvious rates read is that divided government means less spending and relief for the UST long end, but Mizuho cautions against chasing it.
Trump's willingness to deal could bring higher defence spending and some dilution of planned Medicaid cuts, leaving the fiscal trajectory little changed.
Mizuho's US econ estimates imply a contained initial reaction: about +2bp in 10Y yields under a Democratic sweep versus -3bp for a Democratic House and Republican Senate.

Beyond the initial reaction, the election matters for whether fiscal concerns revive UST steepening, and for the AI trade, where tighter regulation under a Democratic sweep could test valuations and extend the rotation out of equities into fixed income.
JOLTS is the main US release, with job openings expected to rise. With the Fed in a vague 'neutral' hold, firm labour demand would make a meaningful front-end rally harder.

USTs bull-flattened Monday as a sharp oil drop unwound part of last week's sell-off. 10Y yields briefly fell below 4.90% and 2s10s went through 30bp. Brent bounced overnight on reports of limited US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island.
In 10s, 4.80% is the first meaningful resistance. A renewed move toward 5% would put the bearish duration story firmly back in play.

EGBs rallied on Monday's energy price collapse. 10Y Bund yields broke below 3.30%, OATs and BTPs outperformed, and the curve flattened out to 10Y. The oil rebound likely limits how far the rally extends today.

About 90% probability of a December ECB hike is priced, which keeps the front end anchored through a busy ECB speaker day. Higher oil is likely to bring bearish pressure back to duration as 10Y Bunds bounce off 3.30%.

Gilts rallied Monday, with 10Y yields below 5.20% and the 30Y swap rate briefly below 5%. Today's £3.25bn Mar-37 Green Gilt auction tests demand at these levels, and Thursday's BoE meeting will show whether the MPC endorses aggressive market pricing.
Asian equities were mixed, with tech weak and the oil rebound weighing on sentiment. Japan was closed. The RBA delivered a dovish hike.
